headline: High: shared filesystem writes and shared-context skills create medium-to-high risks of leakage, conflict, and cascading errors; prompt injection is limited by lack of direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no documented direct ingestion channel from marketingskills, and marketingskills is a skills repo that references shared context rather than a live message bridge. The only plausible bridge is manual file/content transfer or shared workspace use, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by a shared filesystem or copy-paste workflow
IF Airflow parses marketingskills-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic parsing of imported text as instructions
Require human review before reusing outputs
Use provenance labels on transferred files

B_data_leakage.rationale: marketingskills can read and write files and has allowlisted egress, while Airflow has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, content touched by one can flow into the other and then out over network paths. Airflow's touched data classes are empty, so this is inferred from capabilities rather than direct sensitive-data evidence.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory tree
IF either agent processes sensitive files placed in that workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Block outbound egress except approved destinations
Keep sensitive files out of shared workspaces
Add file-level access logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills can read and write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Airflow is a data orchestrator with broad network egress. The pair can contend over shared mutable files or generated artifacts if co-located, and marketingskills explicitly supports multiple instances, increasing collision risk. No locking is documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF either agent mutates shared artifacts without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Add a lock file or mutex around shared writes
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
Make outputs append-only where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around skills that reference each other and build on shared context, so it may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. Airflow can then propagate those outputs into downstream automation or API calls. The interaction is inferred, but the shared-context design makes unverified propagation plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Airflow uses marketingskills output as an input artifact
IF downstream tasks act on that output without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step before downstream use
Require schema checks on exchanged artifacts
Mark generated content as untrusted by default
Log and review any automated follow-on actions

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and Airflow's touched data classes are empty. marketingskills does handle marketing content and product marketing context, so compliance concerns are possible only if regulated data is introduced into that workflow; the other agent is not cited because no such data class is documented.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into marketingskills workflows
IF retention or residency requirements apply to that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of marketing workflows
Document retention expectations for shared artifacts
Review data classification before transfer
Use separate storage for regulated content
